what_was_done: Not edited: rules/step-results.md, topics/hook-platform-facts.md and topics/caller-identity.md are outside the files this round may write, so their text still lags the platform record. What changed: this finding is now the tracked entry for them. It is triaged to the three files and to H7 (the rules unit, which builds step-results) and H1 (the hook runner, which owns caller-identity and is the 'subsystem' whose first build task line 40 of hook-platform-facts.md names), so it stands in by-package/H7.md and H1.md, which those builders read. Step-4 ORDER.md section 7 no longer carries the list: it names this finding, and PR4C-16, PR4C-12 and PR4C-17 for tests-e2e.md and spikes.md, and says the platform record holds over those files until they are edited. story-deliver.md's 'Git hooks run' is vague, not wrong, and stays in the steward's ordinary list there. A third file with the same fault was found and added: topics/caller-identity.md, section 'Not yet proven', still calls items 27 and 28 unproven. rules/auto-allow.md's sentence on item 30 is a pointer whose fallback no longer fires; it is not wrong and is not listed. What each unit does. H7 (rules): build the grounded:false rewrite as proven (platform items 37 and 38): allow plus updatedInput on the second return, with no branch and no test for a platform that ignores it; the plan's test_ungrounded_blocks_once_then_marks (rules.md section 7) already asserts the rewrite and the allow on stdout. H1 (hook runner, built, and hook-runner-b): no code change. The built runner pairs the rewrite with allow and has no fallback; do not build the hash-named marker of caller-identity.md, and do not capture payloads as a first task, since items 27, 28, 30, 36 and 38 hold them. For the spec steward, when a file is next touched or shrinks to a pointer at its built package: (1) rules/step-results.md, step 4: replace its last sentence ('Whether the platform honours ... the tool's verdict stands.') with 'The platform honours the rewrite on a StructuredOutput call in a step, in the default mode, while the finding object stays open ([[topic:platform-proven-2]], items 37 and 38).' (2) topics/hook-platform-facts.md: status of row 27 becomes 'Proven with allow: auto mode in the main session, a dispatched agent and a step ([[topic:platform-proven]], item 27); default mode in a step ([[topic:platform-proven-2]], item 38)'; row 28 'Proven ([[topic:platform-proven]], item 28)'; row 30 'Proven in the default mode ([[topic:platform-proven]], item 30)'; the third column of each becomes 'n/a', keeping its fallback only after 'If a later release changes it:'; line 40 is deleted, because no row is left unverified. (3) topics/caller-identity.md: the section 'Not yet proven' says both facts are proven (items 27, 28 and 38) and keeps its two fallbacks only as what follows if a later release changes that.

agents.md M3 now gives the rule with its reason in one sentence, the words every builder method carries in its Finish: 'If the call is moved to the background, run the same command again: it re-attaches to the job already running and is not a second copy; do not wait for or read the background task.' The clerk's Rules carry that same sentence, and its no-JSON rule now speaks of a finished call, so a moved call, which has printed no JSON, leads to the re-run and not to an error result. Section 7 item 3 adds the check: clerk.md and every method Finish that names a gate hold the sentence. topics/long-commands.md now says that the platform's notice tells the agent the opposite (wait for the result, start no second copy) and that the agent is therefore given the rule together with the reason, in every method that ends with a gate command and in the clerk's rules, checked by a lint test. PR4-2 in extra-probes-4.json says the same, and words E2's check so that it measures (after a call that shows the backgrounding signature, the step's next Bash call is the same command) or says that nothing was measured. Step-5 RESOLUTIONS.md records the change under PR4C-13. To stay under 24,000 bytes (agents.md is 23,991) four restatements were shortened or dropped: D14 and D16 now point to M1 and to frame item 5; the wall-row clause of section 2, which section 3 states; the spike-runner clause of section 1, which D20 states; and the row 'A2b: no ledger file', which held no rule. The evidence. The check's rerun logs still exist, and I read the notice in them: scratchpad chk4/logs/C.jsonl, line 5, the PreToolUse event of the step's StructuredOutput call, into which the step had copied the Bash result; D.jsonl, line 10, has the same words with the sandbox on. Item 43 of topics/platform-proven-2.md now quotes the notice in full with that provenance, so the words are in the repository, and the record's header says that this one line is quoted in the item because CHECK.md does not quote it. Not done, because rewrite/spike/ is outside what this round may write: saving the logs themselves. For the orchestrator, while the session scratchpad exists: copy chk4/logs/C.jsonl and D.jsonl into rewrite/spike/probes-round-4/ (for example a folder check-reruns/), then give item 43's citation that folder and drop the sentence added to the header.
where: rewrite/plans/step-5/agents.md (M3, the clerk in section 3, section 7 item 3); rewrite/spec/topics/platform-proven-2.md (item 43)
